answer: A quiet place I really treasure is a small reading corner in the public library in our town, just a ten-minute walk from our flat. I stumbled upon it by chance a few years ago, when I was looking for somewhere to prepare for my university exams, and I have been going ever since. Tucked away near the back, behind the tall shelves of old newspapers, it is a [[secluded]] little spot that most people seem to overlook. I usually go there to read or study, because the silence helps me concentrate in a way that is impossible at home, where my younger sister is often revising and the television is on in the next room. These days I mostly go on a free afternoon with a novel or a book about business. There is something wonderfully peaceful about being surrounded by books, with only the occasional turning of a page to break the quiet. In our increasingly noisy world, finding somewhere so genuinely [[serene]] feels like a small luxury. I often [[lose track of time]] there, completely [[absorbed]] in whatever I am reading. Honestly, it has become a kind of [[sanctuary]] for me, a place to escape the constant distractions of modern life, and I deliberately leave my phone on silent at the bottom of my bag. I always feel calmer and more focused after spending an afternoon there, and I think everyone deserves a corner like that somewhere in their life.

followUps.q: Do you prefer studying at home or in a library?
followUps.answer: Definitely in a library. At home there are too many distractions, like the television, my phone and family conversations, whereas in a library everyone around me is focused, which makes it much easier to concentrate.

followUps.q: Do many young people in your town use the library?
followUps.answer: Fewer than before, I think. A lot of students now study online or at coaching centres, but during exam season the library still fills up with young people looking for a quiet place to revise.

note: Placed the corner in the town's public library; added how he found it, why home is noisy, phone habit; moved plain 'peaceful' mark to 'sanctuary', added 'lose track of time'.
